summary: Rongdao Lai works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, later serving as an assistant professor there and as a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and later earned a PhD at Harvard University, where his doctoral supervisor was Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey and held a teaching post at International Christian College.

Rosalind O'Hanlon is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (~1978–1983), was an Emeritus Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge (~1983–2008), and served as Professor in Indian History and Culture at Oxford (~2008–2021).

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from 1960 to ~1969. He served as an assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1983–2012) at Komazawa University, and directed the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher and earned an MA at the Free University of Brussels. She was a research fellow at the NFSR (1961–1970) and became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1970.

Rosemarie Fuchs is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and she was a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg. She held professorships at the University of Giessen (1990–1994), the University of Jena (1994–2013), and Humboldt University of Berlin (2013).
Rosemary Radford Ruether was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She studied at the Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965) and held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).

Rosina Pastore specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, serving there as an assistant and PhD candidate, and later became an affiliated researcher at Ghent University.

Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar and Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1989–2023). He graduated from the University of Western Australia (~1963–1967) and studied under Robert Baker Aitken and John Tarrant (1982–1992).

Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies who received his doctorate from Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served on the faculty at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997), chairing the Department of Anthropology, and was president of the American Anthropological Association.

Roy Tzohar works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Tel Aviv University and earned a PhD from Columbia University (~2005–2011) under Gary A. Tubb, later joining the faculty at Tel Aviv University (~2011).

Roy W. Perrett is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Canterbury (~1970–1974) and the University of Otago (~1978–1982). He held posts at Massey University (~1987–2000), the University of Hawaiʻi (~2000–2004), and the University of Melbourne (~2004–2008).

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology. He earned degrees from Harvard and Columbia, where he studied under Donald Keene, and taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, and the Australian National University, where he led the Japan Centre (1990–2000).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and held a post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikidō Takasaki. He held posts at Sophia, Southern Methodist University, and Perkins School of Theology.

Rudolf G. Wagner was a Sinologist who studied at the universities of Bonn, Paris, Munich, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (~1972–1987) and served as a professor at Heidelberg University (~1987–2009).

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and Frederick William University Berlin, later holding a post at Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, later serving at Bonn as an academic staff member (1974–2004) and teaching Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt.
